slides.1.title: Vinho Verde DOC Map
slides.1.description: Vinho Verde is Portugal's largest DOC, with 9 sub-regions in the Minho area; Alvarinho is concentrated in the northernmost Monção e Melgaço
slides.3.title: Monção and Melgaço: The Pinnacle of Alvarinho
slides.3.html:
Monção and Melgaço are the two top sub-regions of the Vinho Verde DOC, right next to Rías Baixas in Spain (the home of Albariño).

🌡️ Microclimate advantages

  • Located along the Minho River and sheltered by mountains, summers are warmer and drier than in other Vinho Verde sub-regions
  • Annual rainfall of 800–1,000mm (lower than elsewhere in Minho) helps Alvarinho ripen fully
  • Granite soils: give a mineral character and fresh acidity

🍾 Alvarinho at its best

  • More concentrated and full-bodied than typical Vinho Verde, with alcohol usually reaching 12–13%
  • Aromas: peach, apricot, citrus, tropical fruit, with pronounced minerality
  • Can be aged in oak, developing creamy stone-fruit complexity (premium wines)
  • Ageing potential of 3–8 years, with top wines reaching 10 years or more

🏆 Well-known producers

  • Soalheiro: the best known in Monção, the benchmark for varietal Alvarinho
  • Anselmo Mendes: a pioneer of the modern style, also makes oak-aged versions
  • Quinta de Santiago: representative of the traditional style
slides.4.title: Overview of the 9 Vinho Verde Sub-regions
slides.4.html:
Sub-region Main grapes Style
Monção / Melgaço ⭐ Alvarinho The richest, most age-worthy top white wines
Lima Loureiro・Arinto Prominent floral notes with bay leaf and honey
Cávado Arinto・Loureiro Fresh and high in acidity, typical Atlantic style
Ave Trajadura・Loureiro Light and aromatic, with citrus notes
Amarante Azal・Arinto Among the highest acidity, with pronounced minerality
Baião Arinto・Vinhão (red) A stronghold of deeply coloured red Vinho Verde
Basto Azal・Rabo de Ovelha Fuller-bodied and fruity
Sousa Vinhão・Espadeiro (red) Mainly deeply coloured, tannic reds
Paiva Blended white varieties The southernmost, light and easy-drinking
slides.5.title: Alvarinho vs. Loureiro vs. Arinto: Comparing the Three White Grapes
slides.5.items.0.desc: The richest, with peach, apricot and tropical fruit, minerality, high acidity and good ageing. Portugal's best-known white grape
slides.5.items.1.desc: Bay leaf blossom, honey and orange blossom; light, elegant and easy-drinking. The soul of the Lima sub-region
slides.5.items.2.label: Arinto (whole region)
slides.5.items.2.desc: The highest acidity with strong minerality, crisp and zesty, often the backbone of blends. Found throughout Vinho Verde and Portugal
slides.6.question: Which sub-region of the Vinho Verde DOC is known for top Alvarinho white wines and regarded as the heart of the whole DOC?
slides.6.explanation: Monção and Melgaço are the top sub-regions of the Vinho Verde DOC, where Alvarinho performs best. Sheltered by mountains, summers are warmer and drier than in other sub-regions, so Alvarinho can ripen fully and is richer and more age-worthy than typical Vinho Verde.
slides.7.question: Why is a little CO₂ traditionally retained in Vinho Verde?
slides.7.options.1: To add freshness, complementing the crispness of high acidity
slides.7.options.2: To mask faults in the wine
slides.7.explanation: The slight natural CO₂ (spritz) in Vinho Verde is a result of traditional winemaking: traditionally it came from malolactic fermentation (MLF) in bottle producing a little carbon dioxide, while today most producers inject CO₂ directly (at pressure below 1 bar, so it is not classed as sparkling wine under the regulations). This spritz adds freshness and crispness and has become the signature of Vinho Verde, making it especially good with seafood.
